catalog_quote: (b) Suprafixation / tone- Whereas English is a stress language, Lumarachi is a tonal language. Marlo (2007). (Okombo 1982:26) notes the basic patterns of tone as: High (H) [/] Low (L) [-] Down stepped [!/] This study will make use of the low (L) and High (H) tone as the basic tone in Lumarachi. In this case, change in tone signify difference in words. For example: Table 17: Tone Word Tone gloss Omulosi HH Whistle LH Wizard Omusala HL Medicine LL Tree Indaa HL stomach LL Lice ... [Marlo & Metz 2025, sec. 2 item (13), p.2] Predictable Marachi has a privative tonal contrast between H and ∅ (“toneless”). See Hyman (2001) on this property throughout Bantu.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lumarachi is classed as a tone language (lexically contrastive H vs L, with downstep) in explicit contrast to English as a stress language; no word-stress position is given. The first-hand tonal descriptions (Marlo & Metz 2025 p.2: 'Predictable Marachi has a privative tonal contrast between H and toneless'; Marlo 2009, 2013) are entirely silent on stress/accent and penultimate lengthening.
new_statements.domain_note: Typological contrast only (tonal vs stress language) in a contrastive-analysis MA project; the statement is the author's own framing citing Marlo (2007) for tonality. No phrase-level or citation-form prosody discussed. Marlo & Metz 2025 note two tonal varieties of Marachi (a 'reversive' speaker vs 'predictable' speakers) but say nothing about stress.
new_statements.first_reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources concern Marachi = Lumarachi/Olumarachi of Butula, Busia County (Glottolog mara1393, ISO lri, JE342). Marlo & Metz 2025 distinguish two tonal varieties within Marachi (speaker BAM of Marlo 2007 with a reversive lexical verb-tone contrast vs. the 'predictable' single-class system of Bruckhaus 2012's and their own speakers). Marlo 2007 additionally covers Nyala-West (Lunyala of Busia), a separate variety not to be conflated with Marachi.

sources.citation: Marlo, Michael R. & Gus Metz. 2025. Predictable tone in Marachi verbs. Handout, 56th Annual Conference on African Linguistics (ACAL 56), University of Minnesota, 15-17 May 2025. 16 pp. (public Google Drive file linked from the author's site)
sources.note: Nothing. First-hand tonal description: 'Predictable Marachi has a privative tonal contrast between H and (toneless)' (p.2, item 13); two speaker groups (Marlo 2007's speaker BAM has a lexical/reversive verb-tone contrast; Bruckhaus 2012's and the 2011/2016 speakers have a predictable system); 8 melodic H patterns. The words stress/accent do not occur; no remark on penultimate lengthening.
